# Configuration

This reference is generated from the settings schema. Each row gives the accepted type, shipped default and implementation reader. Change personal values through the CLI or `data/config/config.json`; arrays replace defaults whole and objects merge by key.

Use [getting started](getting-started.md) for a first installation, [keys](keys.md) for credentials and models, and [memory](memory.md) for recall and audience behavior. `/config check` validates stored overrides. Model credentials and interface secrets are kept outside this settings file.

To update this reference after a schema change, run `node scripts/config-doc.ts > docs/configuration.md`. Edit the prose in `scripts/config-doc.template.md` and the setting definitions in `src/config/schema/`.

## models.agents

Which backend, model, effort, provider and mode each agent runs on, and the named key `opencode` runs on. `src/subharness/routing.ts` reads them at each run, and `/model set` and `/subharness mode` write them. See [Keys and models](keys.md#model-sources).

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `models.agents.via` | map | `{}` | The backend each agent runs through, by agent (`scout`, `server`, `dev`, `watcher`, `thinker`): `claude`, `codex` or `opencode`. An agent with no entry has no route and its runs are refused `subharness-off`. `/model set <agent> <model> --via <route>` writes it | `src/subharness/routing.ts` |
| `models.agents.model` | map | `{}` | The model each agent runs on, by agent. An agent with no entry runs on its backend's own default | `src/subharness/routing.ts` |
| `models.agents.effort` | map | `{}` | The reasoning effort each agent runs at, by agent. An agent with no entry runs at its model's default | `src/subharness/routing.ts` |
| `models.agents.provider` | map | `{}` | The OpenRouter provider each agent on `opencode` is pinned to, by agent, with no fallback. `/model set <agent> <model> --via opencode-harness --provider <slug>` writes it | `src/subharness/routing.ts` |
| `models.agents.mode` | map | `{}` | What each agent may do, by agent: `read`, `write`, `full` or `sudo`. An agent with no entry runs in its default mode (see [Errands](errands.md)). `/subharness mode <agent> <mode>` writes it | `src/subharness/routing.ts` |
| `models.agents.opencodeKey` | string, null | `null` | The named key of `keys.json` that `opencode` runs on. Null while `opencode` has no login. `neptunia subharness opencode login --key <name>` sets it | `src/subharness/routing.ts` |

## models.routes

The chain of routes each model role runs on, the one place a role's key, harness, model and effort live. `src/llm/route-chain.ts` reads it at each request, and a role with no entry has no route. `/model set`, `/model add` and `/model remove` write it. See [Keys and models](keys.md#chains-of-routes).

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `models.routes` | map | `{}` | The chain of routes of each model role, by role (`core`, `memory`, `analyzer`, `vision`, `video`, `embedding`, `speech`, `drawing`, `search`): an array of `{ "via": "api", "key": name, "model": id, "effort": level }` or `{ "via": "harness", "backend": "claude" or "codex", "model": id, "effort": level }`, tried in order. A role's model is the model of its first route. A role with no entry has no route, and an optional role with no entry or an empty array is off. `/model set`, `/model add` and `/model remove` write it | `src/llm/route-chain.ts` |

| `llm.routeEffort` | map | `{ "core": "disabled", "memory": "medium" }` | The effort a route of a role takes when its text names none, by role, on the scale `disabled`, `low`, `medium`, `high`. On an API route `disabled` sends no `reasoning` and a level sends it as `reasoning.effort`. On a harness `disabled` runs the CLI at `low`, its lowest level (`--effort low` for claude, `model_reasoning_effort=low` for codex), and a level runs it at that level. On a claude harness the memory writer also turns `disabled` into `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0`, and a level into a thinking budget of 2,000, 4,000 or 6,000 tokens for `low`, `medium` and `high`, never above half the output cap of the run. Shipped with `core` at `disabled` and `memory` at `medium`. A role it does not name runs at `medium` when it answers in text (`core`, `memory`, `analyzer`, `vision`, `video` and `search`), and `embedding`, `speech` and `drawing` send no effort, because their models take none. An effort the route names wins. Read at each request | `src/llm/chain-client.ts` |

| `llm.cache.models` | array | `["anthropic/"]` | Model id prefixes whose provider accepts the `cache_control` marker | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.hedge.roles` | array | `["analyzer"]` | Roles whose calls are hedged (two concurrent attempts, first to finish wins) | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.hedge.afterMs` | number | `2500` | Milliseconds before the second attempt starts. `0` or below turns hedging off | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.hedge.timeoutMs` | number | `8000` | Milliseconds from the first attempt's start at which both are aborted if neither returned | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.hedge.longTimeoutMs` | number | `20000` | Timeout used when the caller marks the request `long: true` (the route classifier does this for a large channel list) | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.subscription.thinking` | boolean | `false` | `false` turns Claude's native thinking off with `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` and asks Codex for no reasoning summary. Codex has no switch that turns a reasoning model's thinking off. Read at the start of each run | `src/subharness/subscription-client.ts` |
| `llm.subscription.holdMs` | number | `60000` | How long a subscription run whose last step ended on tool calls waits for its next step before its process is killed (ms). Read after each such step | `src/subharness/subscription-client.ts` |

| `wakes.kinds.*.inputTokens` | number, null | `null` | The input token budget of a wake of the kind; unset or null: the loop budget | `src/tools/access.ts` |

## heartbeat

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `heartbeat.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Whether she has a periodic heartbeat wake | `src/behavior/inner/heartbeat.ts` |
| `heartbeat.schedule` | string | `"every 3h"` | When the heartbeat falls due: `every 3h`, `every 90m` or daily UTC times such as `at 06:00,18:00`. `neptunia services heartbeat setup` writes it, and a value that means nothing reads as the default | `src/behavior/inner/settings.ts` |
| `heartbeat.jitterMinutes` | number | `60` | Minutes an interval of the heartbeat moves either way; daily times stay exact | `src/behavior/inner/heartbeat.ts` |
| `heartbeat.tools` | string, array | `"*"` | The tools a heartbeat wake may call: `"*"` for every granted tool or a list of tool names | `src/tools/access.ts` |
| `heartbeat.maxActs` | number, null | `null` | The most actions a heartbeat wake may take; null: no cap | `src/tools/access.ts` |
| `heartbeat.maxTasks` | number, null | `null` | The most errands a heartbeat wake may start; null: no cap | `src/tools/access.ts` |
| `heartbeat.inputTokens` | number, null | `null` | The input token budget of a heartbeat wake; null: the loop budget | `src/tools/access.ts` |

## cli

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cli.paste.collapseLines` | number | `10` | A paste of more lines than this draws as one chip in the chat input. The turn still gets its exact text | `bin/neptunia.ts` |
| `cli.paste.collapseChars` | number | `2000` | A paste of more characters than this draws as one chip in the chat input. The turn still gets its exact text | `bin/neptunia.ts` |
| `cli.mouse` | boolean | `true` | Whether the chat takes mouse reports: the wheel scrolls the transcript, a drag selects transcript text and copies it to the terminal's clipboard, and a click places the caret in the input. Shift with the mouse still reaches the terminal's own selection in most terminals. Read when the chat opens | `bin/neptunia.ts` |
| `cli.bindings` | array | `[]` | Overrides of the chat keys, each `{ context, key, action }`. A collision or an action the context does not allow shows when the chat opens and is not bound. Read when the chat opens | `bin/neptunia.ts` |
